propositions: A mechanism (derive_caused_by) auto-derives caused_by edges by file-level git blame when no explicit --caused-by is supplied; the fallback silently charges escaped defects to ticket origins without provenance markers, making wrong attributions undetectable and worse than absent edges.

The population of closed bugs carrying caused_by edges (88 bugs) was measured: deriver output agreed with recorded edges in 43%, disagreed in 7%, and abstained in 50% (mostly due to no-majority-or-unresolvable failures); this bound cannot distinguish blame-derived from explicitly supplied edges because recorded edges carry no provenance field.

On 8 bugs with independently proven origins (from root-cause records), the deriver scored 0 correct, 1 wrong-target (named innocent producer), and 7 abstained; the single confident answer was demonstrably wrong and caused by the shape unmet-obligation (consumer edited, producer innocent) where file-majority blame names the wrong party by construction.

Defect shapes dominant in this codebase (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions) are structurally hard for file-level blame: hand-run blame over implicated lines misled in several cases, and the deriver cannot distinguish these shapes mechanically to decline attribution.

A recorded edge and a blamed edge are indistinguishable on read due to absent provenance markers in _write_link_event calls, making it impossible for consumers (escape-rate lenses, epic-close floor) to weight or exclude guesses; the fix is a derived:blame|explicit marker, not a smarter deriver.

The fail-closed behavior (50% abstention rate, especially on hard shapes) is working as designed; the residual risk is confident-but-wrong answers in unmet-obligation shapes where shape detection is not observable to the mechanism; the implementable solution is provenance marking for discounting, not deriver behavior change.
